Blue wire near 0 V, completes the circuit

walkthroughs.body_html:
Three wires, three colours. 🔌

Live = brown, around 230 V. Neutral = blue, near 0 V. Earth = green & yellow, a safety wire to the metal case.

The live wire is the dangerous one — it does the pushing.

A fuse is a thin wire in series with the live wire. If too much current flows, it melts and breaks the circuit.

If a fault makes the metal case live, current flows down the earth wire instead of through you. The big surge blows the fuse.

Together, fuse + earth = safe.

UK mains is AC: 230 V, 50 Hz.

AC (alternating current) swaps direction 50 times a second. DC (direct current) flows one way — like from a battery.

Mains is AC because it's easier to transmit at high voltage over long distances.
